findings.summary: A deceptive fake “Robot Verification” malware-scan advertisement obscures the primary content on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, dark-mode and high-contrast screenshots repeatedly show a large fixed panel claiming to scan Windows executables while asking the visitor to confirm their age. It covers content and mimics security software.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the ad vendor and all creatives that impersonate browser or security UI. Do not replace it with another load-time overlay; keep advertising inline and clearly labelled.

findings.summary: Advertising is disguised as a security and age-verification control.
findings.evidence: The overlay uses reCAPTCHA styling, “Robot Verification,” a fake local Windows file path and a moving scan count, but it originates from an advertising iframe. Lighthouse also found unnamed ad links and iframes.
findings.suggestedFix: Terminate the deceptive ad integrations, audit every ad creative and partner, label ads unambiguously, and prohibit creatives that simulate OS, antivirus, CAPTCHA or age-verification UI.

findings.summary: The page exposes visitors to an extreme, opaque third-party advertising footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 32 third-party origins. HAR attributed 57 requests and 4,037,393 bytes to third parties, including numerous opaque ad domains, while Lighthouse found 26 third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove opaque ad chains and push SDKs, inventory and contractually constrain every remaining vendor, minimize data sent before consent, and cap third-party requests/bytes.

findings.summary: Valid internal article, category and submission routes are interrupted by Cloudflare verification.
findings.evidence: Fresh navigations to an article, category, and submit-story route produced “Performing security verification” instead of the requested content; the article mobile screenshot shows the challenge as the entire page.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot-management rules so ordinary browsers and crawlers can reach public pages; use non-interactive, risk-based checks and provide a recoverable fallback rather than challenging every fresh profile.

findings.summary: Loading is slow and visually unstable.
findings.evidence: The trace measured LCP 4.12s; the mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.203. Lighthouse under mobile throttling measured LCP 22.7s, FCP 4.7s and Speed Index 10.3s.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time ad injection, reserve all media/ad dimensions, prioritize the true LCP resource, and defer non-critical scripts and media until after primary content.

findings.summary: The text listing page transfers a disproportionate, poorly prioritised payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 109 requests and 4,485,439 transferred bytes, including a 3.16MB third-party MP4, 49 scripts and 10 parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets. Lighthouse estimated 75KB unused CSS and 386KB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not preload or autoplay third-party video; remove unused WordPress/plugin assets, consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical modules, and enforce cache and page-weight budgets.

findings.summary: Core navigation, ad frames and form controls lack accessible names or valid ARIA.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 0.64 and failed button-name, link-name, frame-title, select-name and aria-allowed-attr; examples include unnamed menu/share buttons, ad iframes without titles and an unlabelled category select.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic labelled controls, add explicit labels and iframe titles, remove invalid ARIA, and hide purely decorative/ad internals from the accessibility tree where appropriate.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified ratios of 3.41:1 for HOT labels, 2.72:1 for primary buttons and 3.72:1 for input text/placeholder against their backgrounds.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace low-contrast palette pairs with tokens meeting at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and essential UI boundaries.

findings.summary: Mobile viewport declarations disable user zoom.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains user-scalable=no viewport directives; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport. This prevents users with low vision from magnifying the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and remove user-scalable=no/minimum maximum-scale restrictions; then verify reflow at 200% and 400%.

findings.summary: Security policy and cookie hygiene are incomplete despite HTTPS.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no Content-Security-Policy or Referrer-Policy. Cookie inspection found naslvq is not Secure and uses SameSite=None. Lighthouse observed an HTTP ad request automatically upgraded to HTTPS.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, Referrer-Policy, Secure/Lax cookie defaults, remove mixed-scheme endpoints, and allowlist only essential third-party origins.

findings.summary: Third-party media and scripts consume far more resources than the text content warrants.
findings.evidence: A mostly text page transferred 4.49MB; a single third-party MP4 used 3.16MB and third parties used 4.04MB overall. The media is initiated without a user request.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate autoplay/background media, load ads only when viewable and consented, cap partner bytes, and prefer static lightweight placements.

findings.summary: The authored site does not honour the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reports body background rgb(239, 207, 120), body text rgb(48, 0, 0), and color-scheme: normal; the screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint page surfaces, text, controls and embedded ad containers with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A non-essential animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, getAnimations() still reports a running 5.5-second animation. The page loads animated advertising without a user gesture.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion media query that removes non-essential animation and auto-advancing/ad motion; retain only necessary state feedback without movement.

findings.summary: The page has no high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast probe found zero prefers-contrast/forced-colors rules. Lighthouse independently found multiple colour-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, preserve visible control boundaries, and use system colours where forced colours are active.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus, accessible control names and touch-target sizing are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found visible controls with outline: none; Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, select-name and target-size, including 20px-high story links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an accessible name, add a strong :focus-visible style, and provide at least 24px by 24px targets with adequate spacing (prefer 44px for primary touch controls).

findings.summary: Third-party scripts throw runtime errors and use deprecated browser APIs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured autoplay NotAllowedError plus two uncaught exitFullscreen TypeErrors, three deprecation warnings and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the offending ad scripts or sandbox them, gate media playback/fullscreen on explicit user action, handle rejected promises, and replace deprecated APIs.

findings.summary: Form assistance and error accessibility are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Search, category and newsletter controls lacked explicit accessible labels in Lighthouse/platform probes; email and search inputs expose empty autocomplete values, and the dedicated submission flow was blocked by a bot challenge.
findings.suggestedFix: Label every field, add appropriate autocomplete tokens, validate after interaction, announce errors through linked messages/live regions, and keep submission state recoverable.

findings.summary: A multilingual English/Hindi site is built predominantly with physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: The document declares en-US but offers Hindi sections; CSS inspection found 432 rules using physical left/right properties versus 17 using logical properties, with no hreflang alternatives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties, declare language on mixed-language content, and expose hreflang for true localized variants so layout and reading order survive bidi/localization.

findings.summary: The live heap is large for a text listing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 453,734 nodes and 27.0MB self size. After ten full-page scroll cycles it contained 459,673 nodes and 27.4MB; growth was modest, but the starting footprint is disproportionate to the core text experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove ad/player SDKs and duplicate frameworks, lazy-initialize non-essential widgets, and establish heap/node budgets for the listing template.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation and sticky chrome changes are abrupt and lack state-aware guidance.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition rules, scroll timelines, anchor-positioning rules or container queries; navigations replace the page abruptly and the header remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: After core safety/accessibility work, add progressive cross-document View Transitions and scroll-state-aware header cues, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Share metadata is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The page provides title, description, canonical, Open Graph text and JSON-LD, but metadata probing found no og:image while twitter:card requests summary_large_image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an accurate, safely cropped Open Graph/Twitter preview image and validate all structured metadata against the visible page.
